title: Data capacity and calculations
starter: A phone advert says 128 GB of storage. Work out roughly how many 4 MB photos that is, and check with a partner.
starterAnswer: Accept any sensible attempt: this is a hook, not an assessment.
Look for the vocabulary from the lesson objectives appearing in students' own words.
Students who are stuck should still write something: the experience will correct it.
starterNote: Take two or three answers, then leave it open. Come back to it in the plenary, when they can answer it properly.

stations.name: What is data capacity?
facts: Capacity is how much data a device can hold, measured in bytes and their multiples.
To work out what you need, calculate one file's size, then multiply by how many files.
Always check whether the answer is wanted in bits, bytes, MB or GB.
stations.challenge: How would you work out how many photos fit on a memory card?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Capacity is how much data a device can hold, measured in bytes and their multiples.
Also credit: To work out what you need, calculate one file's size, then multiply by how many files.

questions.q: What is the first step in a capacity calculation?
questions.a: Work out the size of one file

questions.q: A card holds 64 GB and each photo is 4 MB. Roughly how many photos fit?

stations.name: Image file size
facts: File size (bits) = width × height × colour depth.
Width and height are in pixels; colour depth is bits per pixel.
Divide by 8 for bytes, then by 1,000 for kB and again for MB.
stations.challenge: Calculate the size of a 1,000 × 800 image with a colour depth of 8 bits.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: File size (bits) = width × height × colour depth.
Also credit: Width and height are in pixels; colour depth is bits per pixel.

questions.q: What is the formula for the size of a bitmap image?
A 500 × 400 image has a colour depth of 4 bits. What is its size in bits?

stations.name: Sound file size
facts: File size (bits) = sample rate × bit depth × duration in seconds.
Sample rate is measured in hertz: samples per second.
Stereo doubles it, because there are two channels.
stations.challenge: Calculate the size of 30 seconds recorded at 44,100 Hz with a bit depth of 16.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: File size (bits) = sample rate × bit depth × duration in seconds.
Also credit: Sample rate is measured in hertz: samples per second.

questions.q: What is the formula for the size of a sound file?
A 10-second clip is recorded at 8,000 Hz with a bit depth of 8. What is its size in bits?

stations.name: Text file size
facts: File size (bits) = number of characters × bits per character.
ASCII uses 7 or 8 bits per character; Unicode often uses 16.
Spaces and punctuation are characters too.
stations.challenge: Calculate the size of a 2,000-character message in 8-bit ASCII.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: File size (bits) = number of characters × bits per character.
Also credit: ASCII uses 7 or 8 bits per character; Unicode often uses 16.

questions.q: A 500-character text file uses 8 bits per character. How large is it?
Why is the same text larger in Unicode than in ASCII?
questions.a: Unicode uses more bits per character

stations.name: Scenario practice
facts: Read carefully: what's the file size, and how many files?
Convert at the end, not halfway through.
Show your working: marks are given for the method as well as the answer.
stations.challenge: Complete the three scenarios on your worksheet.
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Read carefully: what's the file size, and how many files?
Also credit: Convert at the end, not halfway through.

questions.q: 300 photos are 3 MB each. Will they fit on a 1 GB memory stick?
questions.a: No: they need 900 MB, which fits, but only just

questions.q: Why should you show your working?
questions.a: Marks are given for the method, even if the final number is wrong

stations.name: Estimating
facts: Rounding helps: treat 1,024 as 1,000 and 44,100 Hz as 44 kHz.
Check the answer is sensible: a photo shouldn't come out as 3 GB.
Compression makes real files smaller than the calculated raw size.
stations.challenge: Why is a real JPEG smaller than the calculated file size?
challengeAnswer: Model answer: Rounding helps: treat 1,024 as 1,000 and 44,100 Hz as 44 kHz.
Also credit: Check the answer is sensible: a photo shouldn't come out as 3 GB.

questions.q: Why is a real photo file usually smaller than the calculated raw size?
Which would double a bitmap image's file size?

final.name: Final challenge: work it out

questions.q: An image is 800 × 600 with a colour depth of 8 bits. What is the file size in bytes?
A 60-second clip is sampled at 20,000 Hz with a bit depth of 16. What is the file size in bits?
A text file has 4,000 characters stored in 16-bit Unicode. How big is it in bytes?

final.note: Students should have predicted these on the worksheet before tapping the star. Mark the prediction, not just the final answer.

exam.q: State the formula for calculating the file size of a bitmap image.
points: Capacity is how much data a device can hold, measured in bytes and their multiples.
To work out what you need, calculate one file's size, then multiply by how many files.
Always check whether the answer is wanted in bits, bytes, MB or GB.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark for a correct answer.

points: File size (bits) = width × height × colour depth.
Width and height are in pixels; colour depth is bits per pixel.
File size (bits) = sample rate × bit depth × duration in seconds.
To work out what you need, calculate one file's size, then multiply by how many files.
Accept any other correct point relevant to the question.
exam.note: One mark per point, to a maximum of 3.

common: Naming a term without saying what it does: most questions need the term and its purpose.
Answering 'it's faster' or 'it's better' with no reason: link it to the characteristic the question is about.
Repeating the question in the answer and stopping there.
